summary: AX-CORE-001 v1.0.0 is approved and frozen for the GLB/USDZ Foundation Release 1 scope.

reviews.name: Creative Review
reviews.reason: The user approved the current identity, emotional tone, and ADLS direction for v1.0.

reviews.name: Technical Review
reviews.reason: All tiers pass loader, hierarchy, animation, triangle, draw-call, texture-memory, file-size, test, build, and audit gates.

reviews.name: Platform Review
reviews.reason: The user accepted local Chromium plus Three.js GLB/USDZ loader validation as the FR1 certification boundary.

reviews.name: Experience Review
reviews.reason: The user approved the current experience; pause-safe motion and monochrome behavior are implemented and tested.

dimensions.name: Function
dimensions.evidence: The live interactive 3D centerpiece is implemented for FR1; static icon and favicon applications remain in the FR2 Identity System scope.

dimensions.name: Accessibility
dimensions.evidence: Pause-safe interaction and monochrome output are implemented, tested, and accepted for FR1.

dimensions.name: Cross-platform
dimensions.evidence: Local Chromium and loader evidence were accepted as the FR1 boundary; broader device certification is not claimed.

dimensions.name: Motion
dimensions.evidence: The idle animation, lifecycle states, pointer response, and pause behavior are implemented and tested.

dimensions.name: Emotion
dimensions.evidence: The user approved the current approachable-intelligence direction.

dimensions.name: Future-proofing
dimensions.evidence: Single-source tiered geometry is reusable; unsupported formats are explicitly deferred until a consumer requires them.

resolvedDecisions.decision: GLB and USDZ only for v1.0; FBX, SVG, Lottie, and WebM deferred until required.
Local Chromium and loader compatibility accepted for FR1; universal device certification is not claimed.

scopeLimitations: Static icon and favicon applications remain part of Foundation Release 2.0.
FBX, SVG, Lottie, and WebM are not v1.0 deliverables.
High-DPR High quality and representative multi-device certification remain follow-ups if later release criteria require them.
